items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: It was actually originated with a band called Bob Dade (PHONETIC) who actually was not a musician. He was the bouncer at the Rum Boogie Club

ctx.x: You had that with your band from the days when you played it with Cee Pee C.P. Johnson and where do you think that particular arrangement originated? You said it was probably before the Cee Pee Johnson band, isn't that right? (inaudible)

It was actually originated with a band called Bob Dade (PHONETIC) who actually was not a musician. He was the bouncer at the Rum Boogie Club on Highland Avenue. That was the name that the club was where the Cee Pee C.P. Johnson Band

originally played, after Cee Pee C.P. Johnson's band left out of there. See, Cee Pee C.P. lost half his band when Lionel Hampton formed his band because I went with Lionel Hampton. My brother was the trumpet player. He went with Lionel Hampton and my -- the baritone saxophone player was Jack MacVeigh, the guy that wrote the tune, "Open the Door, Richard." He went with the Lionel Hampton Orchestra, so that sort of messed up that band by taking half of them and as a matter of fact, Lionel was so forward, he…
